Date: 2026-04-21
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood CSM); Jared Lowe (TidalWave CTO), Priya Menon (Security Lead), Eli Santos (ML Engineer), Dana Ortiz (Platform Ops)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on SSO enablement, audit log retention, and SOC2 evidence sharing. Agreed items: Redwood to share SOC2 artifacts and encryption docs; SE will run a short dedicated-node benchmark; TidalWave to confirm retention and legal hold requirements. Quick follow-up on SSO test plan and RBAC mapping.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted for retention guarantees
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Okay everyone, thanks for hopping on. This is the TidalWave weekly governance check-in, 16:00 Pacific. Quick roll call.
[00:00:08] Jared Lowe: Hey, Jared here.
[00:00:10] Priya Menon: Priya, hi.
[00:00:12] Eli Santos: Eli.
[00:00:14] Dana Ortiz: Dana.
[00:00:16] Maya Chen: Great. From Redwood we have Carlos and Noah as well. I'll let Carlos take the technical status first.
[00:00:24] Carlos Ruiz: Cool. Hi all. Quick TL;DR: dev env tests finished last night, no data leakage observed in the KV cache experiment — though, uh, the auto-transcription said K-V "cash" for me earlier, so apologies if that shows up funny in the notes. We spun up a small dedicated node to run the latency profile; preliminary p95 is around 230ms for 512 tokens with batching off. We're going to run a dedicated short run with the exact prompt set you provided.
[00:00:50] Priya Menon: Quick question on that p95 — can you confirm if the logs from the run include request identifiers and user identifiers? We need traceability in audit logs.
[00:00:59] Carlos Ruiz: Yep, we include request_id and trace_id at a minimum. We can map to an application user_id if you pass the mapping; by default we mask PII in transcripts but we keep a hunting trail for infra traces.
[00:01:12] Dana Ortiz: And retention — what's the retention window for those audit logs? Our legal team sometimes needs 5–7 years.
[00:01:18] Carlos Ruiz: Default hosted retention is 90 days but on Dedicated or Private we can extend to customer-defined retention, including 7 years if that's required. For hosted we'd have to put an archival export in place (S3 export) and we can tie that to your KMS.
[00:01:32] Priya Menon: So for the POC we need to validate the export pipeline and KMS integration. Can Redwood share KMS reference architecture?
[00:01:39] Maya Chen: Yes, that's on our TODOs. I'll send the KMS patterns and the notes about envelope encryption.
[00:01:45] Jared Lowe: Also, SOC2 — you mentioned you could share the evidence package? Our auditing team wants to tick that box before we do any sensitive inference.
[00:01:53] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll share the SOC 2 Type II cover letter and redacted evidence bundle. Carlos, can you attach the compliance packet link?
[00:02:00] Carlos Ruiz: I'll post the link to the shared drive after the call. It will include scoping, control matrices, and our penetration test summary. Note that some artifacts are redacted for third-party vendor data — hope that's okay.
[00:02:12] Priya Menon: That's fine. We mainly need controls around encryption, access, and retention.
[00:02:17] Eli Santos: On SSO — we tried the SAML metadata you sent; we hit an attribute mapping mismatch. Our idp sends email as mailName and Redwood expects emailAddress.
[00:02:28] Carlos Ruiz: Yeah, attribute mapping is a common hiccup. We can be flexible — we support custom attribute mappings in the SSO config and can map mailName -> emailAddress. Also support SCIM for provisioning if you want auto user sync.
[00:02:42] Priya Menon: SCIM would be ideal to keep RBAC consistent. What about group claims — can you map groups to RBAC roles?
[00:02:50] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, group_claim to role mapping is supported. We've seen some IdPs that encode groups as a single string; we have a parser to split on commas or pipe.
[00:03:02] Dana Ortiz: If we enable SCIM, does Redwood store any of the user attributes long-term? We want to minimize storage of PII.
[00:03:09] Noah Patel: Great question. With SCIM we store the minimal set required for auth—email, name, and an internal id; PII is hashed where possible, and you can configure attribute retention policies. For Private deployments you can opt to keep all user data in your directory only.
[00:03:25] Priya Menon: Okay that's useful. For the POC acceptance criteria, our security team wants: 1) SSO working with group-to-role mapping, 2) audit logs with per-request identifiers and retention/export validated, 3) SOC2 artifact review, and 4) encryption at rest and in transit validated. Are we aligned?
[00:03:43] Maya Chen: That matches what we discussed last week. We'll treat those as the checklist for sign-off.
[00:03:49] Jared Lowe: There's one more: legal needs to confirm that Redwood's subprocessor list is OK. Can you confirm your subprocessors and any planned changes in the next 90 days?
[00:04:01] Carlos Ruiz: We maintain a subprocessor list; I will include the latest list in the compliance packet, and we commit to 30-day notice for changes to subprocessors.
[00:04:10] Priya Menon: About audit logs again — does Redwood provide an immutable audit trail? Our auditors ask for tamper-evidence.
[00:04:18] Carlos Ruiz: We have append-only logs with checksums and can write log digests to a write-once S3 bucket or to a customer-managed ledger in your cloud for higher assurance. For Private, you can host the storage.
[00:04:34] Eli Santos: For the benchmark run, if we see a p95 spike under load, what's the typical mitigation? Autoscale? Falling back to a lighter quantized model?
[00:04:42] Carlos Ruiz: Right, mitigation strategies: autoscale, route to lower-cost/latency models with compatibility, or enable prefix caching. For the POC we can run experiments with and without prefix caching to measure quality delta.
[00:04:55] Priya Menon: Is there any leakage risk when using prefix caching? I'm thinking about shared cache entries across tenants.
[00:05:03] Carlos Ruiz: No cross-tenant cache leaks — cache shards are per-tenant. But if you do share a large model variant across teams, we can configure per-workspace cache namespaces.
[00:05:13] Dana Ortiz: One of our compliance quirks is legal hold — we sometimes need to stick data beyond retention. How would Redwood handle a legal hold request for particular conversation transcripts?
[00:05:23] Noah Patel: We support object-level legal holds on archived exports and can tag specific request_ids to prevent deletion. If you need in-system holds, that's available on Dedicated/Private deployments where you control the retention manager.
[00:05:36] Priya Menon: Good. On encryption — can you call out KMS integration specifics? Our standard is customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS KMS and cross-account key policies.
[00:05:46] Carlos Ruiz: We support CMKs, and for hosted we can do envelope encryption where the data key is wrapped by your CMK. For Dedicated we can mount a customer KMS endpoint or use your HSM via a proxy. We'll provide a reference ARN and sample policy.
[00:06:02] Jared Lowe: Great. Anything unexpected from the POC data so far?
[00:06:06] Carlos Ruiz: Nothing alarming. We did see two error spikes correlated with a malformed prompt that retried rapidly; we've added rate-limiting on retries in the test harness and increased circuit-breaker sensitivity.
[00:06:20] Eli Santos: Okay. On the action item for the benchmark — can Redwood produce a csv with per-request latency, request_id, token_count, and model_variant? That will help our telemetry team ingest it.
[00:06:31] Carlos Ruiz: Yes — we'll produce a CSV and also a condensed JSON summary.
[00:06:36] Priya Menon: If you're sending logs to our S3, do you support SSE-KMS?
[00:06:41] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, server-side encryption with your KMS (SSE-KMS) is supported. We'll show config snippets in the doc.
[00:06:48] Maya Chen: Quick recap before we wrap — Maya: Redwood to send SOC2 packet, KMS architecture and envelope encryption notes (Maya), Carlos to run trimmed benchmark and upload CSV with per-request data (Carlos), Noah to produce SSO test plan and sample SCIM mapping file (Noah). Priya will confirm retention and legal hold specs and share with Maya.
[00:07:07] Priya Menon: Yep that's right.
[00:07:09] Dana Ortiz: Can we get the dedicated-node run scheduled for Thursday? We have a quiet window then.
[00:07:15] Carlos Ruiz: We can do Thursday 03:00 UTC — I'll schedule and post a calendar invite.
[00:07:21] Jared Lowe: One last thought — any red flags on the contract side about required 7-year retention and connectivity for the KMS? Our legal says if Redwood enforces key rotation that would complicate long-term archives.
[00:07:33] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include key rotation policy and long-term archive recommendations in the packet; for long-term archived exports we recommend customer-managed KMS so rotation is under your control.
[00:07:44] Eli Santos: Thanks all.
[00:07:46] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and the next run details.
[00:07:50] (call ends)
